gen-fs-oswald-gf-scope-one: Compact strength meets soft spill. Oswald sets tightly knit rows, strong and confident. Scope One, a classic serif with counters that spill into the surrounding space and stubby ascenders beside a big x-height, would read in a relaxed, traditional way over many lines.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-slabo-13px: Tightly knit rows give Oswald its confident, strong look, and the bookish Slabo 13px follows with large open counters in its tall a, e and s. And its rounded letters stay clearly open, a dignified foil.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-suwannaphum: Dignified and editorial, Suwannaphum has a high x-height like a squared-off woodblock letter. Across a full page, its text serif shapes, with a c as open as a bent paperclip, would feel sturdy and unhurried beside Oswald.
gen-fs-oswald-mulish: Oswald's most distinctive trait is its tightly knit rows, giving the heading a confident, strong look, while Mulish keeps a modern, approachable line with a large x-height. Over a long page, its sans would feel smooth and ruler-straight.
gen-fs-paquito-fs-supreme: Supreme reads crisp, with letters held open rather than curled shut. Paquito, a sturdy and warm serif whose lowercase fills the line like capitals, sits above a body whose heavy-looking strip of text would carry a long page steadily.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-fs-bespoke-sans: Fast and aggressive, Ethnocentric pushes its letters apart. Bespoke Sans stays sharp and refined, with generous space between curve ends and stems that lets whole paragraphs flow along without snagging.
gen-dafont-hammerhead-fs-bespoke-sans: Authoritative, flat-lined Hammerhead looks like fineliner on paper, its wide-open e never squeezed shut, and it hits hardest at display size. But Bespoke Sans is the sharper, finer reader, giving curve ends plenty of room.
gen-dafont-over-there-fs-supreme: Supreme sets a thick, heavy-looking strip of sans text with its letters held open, under the fixed-nib, vintage-military look of Over There. Crisp throughout, it carries paragraphs without tiring the eye.
